title: C339 — Inline connector reading guide
introduction:
This inline connector reference brings passenger-seat power, sensing, communication and restraint circuit labels together. I start by choosing the correct gender and harness heading before reading any cavity row. Matching plug shapes can play mirror tricks; the printed labels are the reliable landmarks on the page.

Each face has its own identity table, drawing and assignment table. Locate the cavity label in that face’s drawing, then read across its matching row for Circuit Number, Color, Gauge, Function, Qualifier, Used and Terminal Part Number. The male drawing places the lower-numbered group on the left; the female drawing places it on the right. Gray-filled circles correspond to rows with blank circuit and function entries. Unlabeled housing projections show shape, without establishing how anything releases.

Keep the face tables separate. Some corresponding rows name different networks or restraint components, and their applicability is unresolved. Matching cavity labels alone cannot settle those differences. Where a supply function names a fuse or circuit breaker, retain both protection alternatives.

This is an identification and reading guide. It supplies no physical viewing-side label, access instructions, restraint depowering sequence or probing procedure. Gauge and Size conventions and a Used-code legend are also unspecified; preserve those entries without using them to select wire or test equipment.

edits.why: I check gender and harness identity together before using the drawing. Its lower-numbered group is on the left and its higher-numbered group is on the right; that describes the illustration’s layout, without establishing a physical terminal-side or wire-side view.

Read each cavity across its own row to distinguish seat power, sensing, network, ground and restraint functions. Preserve the restraint polarity symbols and the separate ground descriptions. These labels identify connections without supplying operating measurements or test instructions.

The numbered groups reverse left-to-right relative to the male illustration. I use this face’s labels and identity table together rather than mentally copying the other drawing’s positions. The projecting housing features have no stated release function.

This table has its own supply, ground, network and restraint descriptions. Preserve its fuse-or-circuit-breaker alternatives and polarity symbols. Differences from the male table remain visible; the available evidence cannot reconcile the competing network and restraint-component assignments.

Keep each kit’s service part, engineering shell, material, gauge and cavity fields together as a separate catalog entry. The two entries for the female shell have different gauge and service-part fields; sharing a shell number does not establish interchangeability or select a repair kit. These listings do not provide installation instructions.

The Product Id is a separate regional catalog listing. The table does not associate it with a particular kit row above or supply installation instructions; do not infer either association from its placement.

originalAuthorHold: At cavities 14 and 15, the male table identifies front-passenger seat-mounted side-airbag circuits CR105/RR105, while the female table identifies passenger-side inflatable-curtain circuits CR111/RR111. No qualifier explains these competing component assignments.

At cavities 5 and 6, the male table identifies VDB04/VDB05 as high-speed CAN, while the female table identifies VDB25/VDB26 as high-speed CAN 2 (UPPER). Confirm applicability before presenting the tables as a verified connection between those network identities.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 72 primary units, four complete pages/two figures and six edits. Original first CLI author covered 61 units/four headings. Complete draft adds pigtail and European catalog headings, all table rows and raw text coverage. Original partial author retained separately; physical network and restraint identities remain unresolved for bounded source reading only.
